---
title: Monolith
description: pouryakit-monolith, the single-Module start that grows into the modular monolith when a second Module arrives.
---

## What it is

`pouryakit-monolith` generates one Host with one Module's data and rules: the Proving Sample's Catalog and `Catalog.Contracts`, behind the Kit's HTTP pipeline, beside projects for its Reverse proxy and its service defaults and a smoke test. Its endpoints send through `IDispatcher`, and the Host registers Catalog on its own services with `builder.Services.AddCatalog()`.

<Callout type="warn" title="One Module in all but name">
  The monolith leaves out `PouryaKit.Modularity`, so the Host holds one Unit of Work: one Module's data. Its Operations name no Module, and its declarations belong to the application. A second Module is the modular monolith's composition.
</Callout>

## When to use it

When the application starts with one business boundary. It is where a project of one Module starts, not a limit on it: the same Catalog code runs in the modular monolith.

## Generate and run it

<Steps>
<Step>

### Generate it

```bash title="Terminal"
dotnet new pouryakit-monolith -n Acme.Shop
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Run it

[Your first Host](/docs/get-started/first-host) starts PostgreSQL, migrates Catalog, creates a token, runs the Host and calls it.

</Step>
<Step>

### Grow it when a second Module arrives

Add `PouryaKit.Modularity` and turn Catalog's Composition Root into an `IModuleDefinition`; [Add a Module](/docs/get-started/add-a-module) shows the path.

</Step>
</Steps>

## What it composes

| | Stated in |
| --- | --- |
| Every Capability its projects reference, and no `PouryaKit.Modularity` | [What each composition composes](/docs/capabilities/templates#what-each-composition-composes) |
| The same composition and startup checks as a Host of Modules, from `AddPouryaKitCompositionChecks` | [What each composition composes](/docs/capabilities/templates#what-each-composition-composes) |
| Nine files that change when Catalog becomes a Module | [Growing the monolith](/docs/capabilities/templates#growing-the-monolith-into-a-modular-monolith) |

## Failure messages

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="A ConfigureContainer of the Host's own">
    The monolith calls `AddPouryaKitCompositionChecks()` last, so a `ConfigureContainer` added before it keeps the container validation and the checks. Keep that order when you add one.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="403 Tenant.Required">
    Catalog is tenant-scoped: a token without the `tenant` claim is refused by every Catalog command and query.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>
